findings.title: Guard the missing destination calendar before reading its integration
findings.body: When a booking uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`. This condition dereferences `.integration` and throws before the booking can be created. The previous check safely handled a missing destination calendar, so ordinary Meet bookings without a configured calendar now fail.

findings.title: Fall back to the event's selected calendar when updating
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this search compares every calendar's `externalId` with `undefined`, so it cannot select the configured destination calendar. `calendar.events.update` then receives an undefined `calendarId` and fails. This breaks updates for bookings whose calendar reference has no external calendar ID, including reschedules and location changes.

findings.title: Delete from the configured destination calendar when no external ID is passed
findings.body: If `externalCalendarId` is absent, the lookup compares calendar IDs with `undefined` and returns no calendar. The subsequent fallback uses `primary`, even when the event was created on a non-primary destination calendar. Cancellation can therefore leave the actual event behind and may target the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Use the destination matching this credential for the organizer address
findings.body: Collective bookings pass the full destination-calendar array to each credential's `createEvent` call, but this code always uses the first destination's external ID as the organizer's email. For every host after the first, Google receives the wrong organizer address in the attendee payload; the event can be attributed to another host instead of the calendar owner.
